The worst airline there is. They lost my bag in a 1.5 hours flight. They gave the wrong address to the courier and made me lose one day of work to try and find my bag.

BA Euroflyer from Gatwick - Kalamata, Greece 30 May 2026 and return 8 days later. BA changed the flight from LHR to LGWK which meant an extra hour on our journey to the airport each way. Flight to Kalamata: was late departing but made up most of the time. We pre-ordered toastie sandwiches, Duty Free Bacardi and a drink each. No drinks were loaded, and BA charged us for buying on board as they "weren't allowed" to give us a free drink in lieu of the ones not loaded. We eventually got a refund. Flight back to LGW was uneventful but virtually no food was loaded on the plane for the journey. At least we had a middle seat free to 'stretch' out in. Good points? Well, the over head lockers/bins were spacious and had plenty of room for our hand baggage. Bad points? Inadequate catering, missing, paid for beverages, unbelievably cramped and uncomfortable seats. We would not recommend BA shorthaul unless they're the only airline that fly to where you want to go.

Very disappointing experience with the boarding gate staff at Heathrow. I accidentally joined the wrong boarding queue because I didn't understand the boarding group system. Instead of politely explaining it, the gate agent interrupted me, spoke to me disrespectfully, and even threatened to remove me from the flight when I questioned her attitude. Also, British Airways is not a budget airline, but for a 2 and a half hour flight, they were charging the passengers for soft drinks as well. No food included. There are many better airlines in the world. I would highly recommend taking those instead.

On a flight from Phoenix to London, we had reserved and paid for seats 58J and 58K. There were only two seats in that row, which is precisely why we selected and paid for them. At boarding, we got an unpleasant surprise: we found ourselves in a three-seat row, with an additional 58H seat. As a result, I had to spend the entire flight in the middle seat, with another passenger sitting on my left. What was the point of paying extra to reserve two seats if we ended up in exactly the same situation as passengers who paid nothing for seat selection? British Airways claims that it did not change our seat numbers and therefore refuses to refund us. This is why I consider this a seat reservation scam by British Airways. I travel frequently to the United States, and British Airways has lost my business because of this experience. I encourage other travelers to do the same and refuse to be misled by airlines that do not take their seat reservation commitments seriously.
Boarding in Nice was a bit messy, as they never called our group (#5), the last one. New aircraft, with a reasonable pitch, and huge space for hand luggage.

I flew British Airways on May 2026 from Chicago to Larnaca, Cyprus via London Heathrow and it was by far the worst flight of my life, all due to unforced errors, omissions, carelessness and just not caring. It started with British canceling my return flight from Larnaca to London. I received an email that that particular leg of my trip had been canceled. No rebooking, nothing. I had to use the British Airways app and try to find an alternate return flight myself. When I called British Airways they didn't apologize and they just matter of fact said that my only option was to return on a flight that left several hours after my original flight. They were proceeding to rebook me when I myself noticed that taking that new flight would make me miss my connection to Chicago in London so I made the agent aware of that, to which she replied "you'll have to stay overnight in London". No apology, no offer to get my a hotel. I accepted the fact and booked a night at the only (and expensive) airport hotel in terminal 5 (Sofitel). So I went on my trip. Onboard service was very subpar and wifi was only available to first class passengers. The day of my return to Chicago I get to the Larnaca airport, check in, go through immigration and proceed to my gate to board my flight to London. When I'm about to board and enter the jet bridge the agent scans my passport and denies me boarding saying that I don't have a UK "ETA" visa. I had no idea that I needed that, plus originally I was never going to stay overnight in London. British Airways should have told me that I needed that ETA the moment that they forced me to stay overnight in London due to their canceling my original flight! And they should have never allowed me to check in and get all the way to the gate I needed a visa for the UK. I get denied boarding and then an airport agent had to escort me back through Cyprus immigration and I had to secure transportation back to Nicosia (about 40 minutes away) and accommodation for that night. Then I had to apply for a UK ETA visa and come back the next day for yet another attempt to get to the UK. So the next day I come back to the airport with my UK visa, board my flight and still had to spend a $300 hotel night in London because my connection departed the next day. All I'm trying to do is make a simple connection, and all you had to do was provide the bare bones minimum expected customer service. Huge fail. I will avoid British Airways like the plague from now on.
Almost faultless flight. Food and wine at B Gates Galleries lounge good. An exceptional crew, only food let the flight down a bit, otherwise very enjoyable, on time.

Great service from the cabin crew, disappointed to be on a 777 instead of the A350 we flew out from LHR on ten days before. The 777 is noisier than the A350, Food and service were very good. The only issue was the broken headphone socket. Clearly not something the crew could fix, and I hope BA got it sorted at Heathrow. Luckily, there was one empty seat, and I was able to transfer to it after take off. I have been critical of BA and its product in the past but our last four flights have been very good indeed. Pretty fair choice on the IFE but the Panasonic map was slow and limited in scope. Shame BA does not have the external cameras certain other carriers have.

Flight from London to Gothenburg was overbooked. We were not informed but could not check in online, first red flag. At the airport in Edinburgh we check in to problem, no one told us about the situation and that we could not get seats on the next flight. At the help desk in Heathrow we wanted to get our seats, no one told us the situation, just to go to the gate. Rushed through security and through the terminals since our first flight was delayed. With 5 minutes to spare at the boarding gate we were told we had no seats and that the flight had took off. After 2-3 hours with the service personnel we got a hotel room and a new flight home the next day. We were also told that we could get our bags at the BA desk near baggage claim. At baggage claim they told us that BA could not get our bags since their were sent to SAS (our new flight home) but we could fetch them at their respective desk. When at SAS they were not able to help us and basically told us that only BA could fetch our bags. After given up this wild goose chase we went to the hotel without any toiletries or spare clothes. We had to beg in the hotel reception for some basic hygiene products and spare underwear if they had them, quite humiliating. 24 hours later then planned we were back home. During this whole process you basically had to beg for anything to happen, get a new flight, get a hotel, get anything. We learned after the fact about our rights to compensation for example. At no step of the way were we a priority nor did they inform us of anything, we had to ask and know what to ask. This was a really stressful experience and is seems unnecessary that this should have happened at all. They should have informed us from the get go and let us get ahead of the situation and perhaps get ahead of it themselves and prepare everything for us to make the best of a bad situation but of course that is not how it went. Now starts the process of getting reimbursed for extra expenses and claim the compensation with have a 4-8 week turn around according to British Airways.

Outstanding flight on British Airways. The crew were attentive, professional and welcoming. Good and welcoming information from the flight deck, too. Food and wine selections were very good. Dinner was excellent and attractively presented. The lie flat seat was very comfortable and I managed about five hours of sleep. BA at its best.

Not Verified After the huge let down of BA downgrading the frequent flyer status of a lot of people including us, loyal and regular travellers, I probably wasn't feeling all that enthusiastic about BA. In the event the flight went smoothly and the food was good enough. However on a well over ten hour flight it's not good enough not to have a proper drinks service mid flight. Ten hours is a long time to go without more than the drink you have with your meal. This would have avoided the never ending stream of passengers going to front to ask for a drink with their begging bowls. It's all very low-cost.
BA575 Flight was delayed by 2 hr 30 min on 13th May and no complementary snacks were given. Even for purchase no sandwich was available and USB charger was not available.

Flew first class qand there was food residue from the previous flight. Service only at times, I went to the galley nd no one present. Went to business class galley and grabbed a bag of chips - staff told me I cannot take such and to go back to my seat. For afternoon tea I asked for a cheese tray I did not have after dinner but not available any longer. WiFi was not available.

I'm not entirely sure as to what they wish to achieve by reducing the seat pitch. I know it's a fairly short flight, but some of us are over 1.80mts tall. If you do online check-in at Vienna there is no 'bag drop' for hold luggage, so the option is fine if you're only carrying cabin baggage. And by the time the 'bag drop' counter is opened, the normal check-in desks are open anyway. As part of the frequent flyer programme, we will still use you (and associates), but please improve on the above issues.

Our first time in the new business class cabin and a great improvement over the old reverse herringbone seat. Pleasantly surprised at the food quality on this flight. The sleep pack consisting pillow, quilt and mattress could have been very good as the pillow was large and comfortable and the quilt was quite good enough for the purpose. However, the mattress was truly appalling. Extremely thin and way too small for the seat. No use whatsoever. Such a shame. The amenity kit was about on a par with most European and US offerings. Small, plastic pouch with socks, mask and a couple of minute tubes of lotion and lip balm. If that is the best they can do, why bother? 90% positive though, a big improvement.

Highly commendable again on all fronts for the short 35 minute flight to LHR. Very efficient service including delivery of a light and tasty dinner which was more than satisfactory considering the duration of the flight. Friendly cabin crew who were more than happy to serve 2 glasses of champagne in that time and despite all the people they had to serve, had time to chat to customers.

Highly commendable on all fronts for the short 35 minute flight. Efficient boarding and service including delivery of a light and tasty breakfast plus hot drink which was more than satisfactory considering the duration of the flight. Friendly and efficient service from the cabin crew.

T5 lounge fairly good. We got bulkhead seats for both legs. Seats not particularly comfortable. Food pretty inedible. Staff good. We're silver so able to book seats, good price for fare. In flight entertainment grim on outbound leg.Went hand baggage only, which was excellent at Nashville airport.

Check in was efficient. Lounge was good with great food and good beverages. The toilets in the BA lounge at Cape Town are noticeably cleaner than they are in their Lounge at T5. Boarding was efficient. I love the muted colours of BA business class. Everything in the seat worked with the minor exception of scratching and popping from the headphones if you jiggled the cable. Drinks came promptly. I had a fantastic cabin attendant who had perfect old school charm. What a delight he was. So good that I have found the page on the BA website where you can compliment someone and I have done so. The food out of Cape Town is Newrest and not as good as the Do & Co out of Heathrow. My soup was served lukewarm. My main was OK. IFE worked fine. Great nights rest. Bags arrived promptly. I deduct a point for being served cold soup and a point for the two flight attendants chatting away who kept me waiting a long time to get past them even though one could see i wanted to get to the toilet. It was not work related chat but middle of the night gossip. I have flown Singapore Business recently and this would never happen.

I am close to retaining Bronze status for the next year. My Tier points collection ends on 31st March 2026. I took a return flight from London to Buenos Aires with their partner Iberia. I claimed the tier points and Avios for the outbound flights. They came in less than a week. I claimed the points for the return flights a month ago but nothing has come. I tried chat (no help whatsoever) and the online form (no answer ever) They have deliberately delayed my points and will apply them no doubt immediately after 31st March 2026 so I get pushed back to Blue status. British Airways hates anyone who travels Economy to be anything but Blue. I tried to transfer some Vueling Avios to British Airways but it didn't work. I contacted them too but of course no reply. Do not join their Club.

I recently flew Business Class on BA95 from London to Montreal. Despite paying a premium price for a modern Business Class experience, I was provided with an ancient 2-4-2 "Ying-Yang" cabin layout. This configuration offers zero privacy, requires jumping over other passengers' legs, and is entirely inconsistent with the "Club Suite" product British Airways markets. To make matters worse, there was no WiFi connectivity for the duration of this international flight. When I raised these issues, British Airways acknowledged the "inconvenience" but offered no compensation.

Lounge in Miami was pretty good (much better than the terrible lounge at LHR). Seat layout in business is shockingly bad. For the middle seat you have to clamber over other passenger's legs to get out. If they have their seat down to rest/sleep. Seat design is unbelievably poor. No storage space, apart from a drawer, which you cannot access with the seat flat. No screen on the outside seats, so you are continuously subjected to disturbance from passengers/crew walking past. No place to put blankets or pillows, etc. when they are not being used. Toilet was filthy and not checked during the 8 hour flight. Crew uniform is awful for the ladies, either trousers with an apron over the top, which looks like a school dinner lady, or ill fitting skirt and top. The flight took off and arrived on time. But the leg from LHR to Madrid to Puerto Rico was cancelled. Not sure why, given Madrid is nowhere near the war zone, but BA is always cancelling flights due to lack of resources.

Lost my suitcase. Cramped cabin with a seat pitch of 29 inches. The food was overly salted chicken breast full of tendons. The experience was diabolical, with a cheap and nasty feel to the entire dining experience. Waited one hour at luggage carousal to then find my suitcase left behind.

A fairly horrendous experience. Our flight at 18:10 was cancelled just before 20:00. Prior to being unloaded we had to endure a cold, awful meal which I think was an attempt to save money. Left to our own devices and back to the airport the next day. You would have thought the ground crew were the victims, miserable, rude and abrupt. Having to eat the exact same meal again, which was even worse 24 hours later, was awful. The crew spent practically the whole flight chatting and catching up, and nothing in "raid the larder:. To add insult to injury our first online compensation claim was reviewed and closed with 24 hours, the second one even quicker. No promised e-mails giving us details of the outcome. I've resorted to old school tactics and sent a recorded post claim. Fingers crossed. They really don't make it easy to be liked.

Food was ok staff were good. There were a few seats on the plane broken. Paid for extra leg room seat but it would not recline. Spoke to the steward during the flight who was very helpful. He said that he would lodge a complaint with customer relations and I would get a refund for the extra I paid to select the seat since it was broken. Customer relations contacted me and said no refund would be given the plane got me to my destination. Very disappointed they don't honour what their staff say. Won't fly with them again.

Avoid the BA Cityflyer Embraers Flew from STN to FLR on Feb 8. Funny smell on the plane, which was quite unpleasant, seats rock hard and don't recline, limited legspace. The only plus points of the flight was the very cheap price, getting airbridged onto the plane (a rarity at Stansted) and the friendly enough crew. Also, these Embraers are based at London City.

This BA flight on 31 Jan was largely uneventful. The food service has deteriorated further. The seats in economy as uncomfortable as ever. BA crew are generally quite efficient but there's something very snooty and superior about BA staff which you don't see on many other airlines. It's hard to explain but it's almost as though they're there to do you a huge favour when in reality you're keeping them in a job and in many cases could fly with another airline. I've always resisted it when people have claimed this before but sadly I do believe it's true.

Had a great time in lounge at Gatwick, a much nicer experience than Heathrow. A good flight with an above average cabin crew, unfortunately let down by the old style club world seats. The awful climbing over someone's legs to use the bathroom.

I have been flying with BA for many years now, and it has always been a premium and comfortable experience. However, my recent experience with them has shown a worrisome sign. First, we have to board the flight from the outdoor platform, which is common for cheaper budget flights. Second, the wifi is not working for this trip. Lastly, we are waiting on the flight for 20 mins.

Every single aspect of my recent journey from Gatwick to Las Palmas had major flaws. I tried to check in at the Club check in and was turned back at the entrance to the Club check in as there were "luggage issues". Nowhere to go or sit, so I had to stand in the departures hall for 45 minutes which was very chilly and I was not dressed for the cold. Eventually checked in andwent through to the BA lounge which was really full and struggled to find two seats together. Then went down to board the plane and no priority boarding so had to join a long queue to access the plane. On the plane it became obvious pretty quickly that all the supplying for food and alcohol had gone badly wrong. The food item I wanted for my main course was finishied so i asked for a cheese board and some red primitivo wine. Then found out no Primitivo wine left. Nobody in rows 11 or 12 got their wine with their lunch and by 14.23 (two hours into a four plus hour flight) the plane was out of "still" wine completely. The CSD was hugely apologetic but clearly it was not his mistake the plane did not have enough of anything. I had received a communication form BA recently proudly announcing the fact that the Internet would be available for free. Great but the internet went down after less than an hour and stayed off for the rest of the flight. Apparently this is pretty normal! We did land 20 minutes early which was great and then our luggage took ages to arrive on the conveyor belt. So much for priority luggage tags which clearly don't work very well. The crew were all lovely but it was a shocking waste of my money to pay for Club. I could have had the same journey for masses less money in economy .(or travelled on Ryanair)! I actually left the plane hungry. Regrettably I have already booked to do the same flight with BA again in April and am now regretting booking the flight. I could go on Ryanair / EasyJet for almost nothing and get almost nothing but save loads of money. I will not be booking any more flights with BA. When are BA executives going to learn that if you sell 15 plus rows of Club seats / you need the right number of staff and the right amount of food and alcohol - this is not the first experience I have had of exactly this situation on flights to and from Las Palmas.. In fact it has been pretty much the same experience every time I have travelled to or from Las Palmas.The return flight from Las Palmas to Gatwick can be much worse if there is no more food and wine loaded at Las Palmas which has happened. I don't normally bother to spend hours writing reports on my flights as I really have better things to do with my time, but this experience was definitely noteworthy. After escalating my complaint to the senior complaints team at BA , I was offered a small amount of Avios points as compensation for the really poor experience. I replied saying I thought this was underwhelming and got a reply saying they had no legal obligation to give me anything and this was a full and final gesture. I am now considering contacting my Credit Card company after I have flown back to Gatwick and asking for a charge back for non delivery of the promised services. Will be interesting to see where this goes to.

I have not used BA for 15 years and the experience was abysmal as before. The plane was one hour late departing because they are unable to prepare the plane in a competent manner. The seat was the most uncomfortable I have encountered in any European flight. The pitch is 29 inches meaning that if you are over 5 foot, 7 inches your knees will be forced into the seat in front.

My family and I have been treated like garbage by them over the past few days. Our main issue relates to their insane policy that works as follows: when travelers are stranded at Heathrow (and presumably other airports) for multiple days because of BA, BA only gives them a hotel voucher for the first night of being stranded. BA requires travelers to return to LHR the next day to retrieve a voucher for that second night, and the voucher can require them to move to a new hotel, for no reason, even when their current hotel has availability. This happened to my family this week when we were traveling from Milan to Washington via LHR. BA delayed our flight from Milan Linate to LHR by about 2 hours, which meant that my wife, children, and I missed our connection. This happens, and it's a part of travelling. We had to wait in a queue for 3 hours for rebooking and hotel information. When we finally got to speak to a BA rep (around 8 pm), he informed us that we had been rebooked on a flight 48 hours after our original flight (meaning that we would be stranded in London for two nights) and then issued us a hotel voucher for 1 night. I thought this was a mistake, but he explained that BA has a policy that requires passengers to return to the airport the next day to get a voucher for that day. He agreed that the policy made no sense and created misery for passengers, but he was powerless to do anything about it. So we went to the hotel, and the next morning I left my family at the hotel and took the Tube back to the airport to request a voucher for our second night in London. I walked into Terminal 5 and started asking any BA rep I could find to direct me to the right desk for hotel vouchers. One sent me to Area D, but that was wrong. Area D's agent sent me to Area H, but Area H was unable to help. I found another agent who told me he had overheard another passenger asking about hotel vouchers, and said that if I waited with that passenger, another agent would probably come out and then I could ask her for help. This actually worked.... although it exposed the fact that there is absolutely no organized system at LHR for assisting passengers who return to LHR to collect vouchers in compliance with BA's insane policy. The agent came out and asked me to write my confirmation number and name on a Post-It note. The agent took her Post-It notes "to the back" and returned about 20 minutes later with vouchers for a different hotel. Every single passenger in the group I was in was re-assigned to a different hotel than they were currently in, even though each of us (and we were actually all at different hotels) had confirmed that our current hotels had plenty of availability and were able to keep us in our same rooms. I told the agent that this made no sense and that our hotel could accommodate us, but she said we had no choice, and that BA reserves the right to make passengers move hotels even if there is availability where they were initially assigned. Rather than repack my famiy and move miles away to a new hotel, I ended up paying out of pocket to remain in our current rooms (for 114 GBP a room). BA's policy here seems designed to torture passengers... and even the BA reps seem to recognize how appalling and nonsensical the policy is.

Poor baggage handling. Delayed from Phoenix to London then delayed from London to Manchester. Told cases were delayed but both would be on next flight. 1 case turned up. Then told that the next case would be on the flight the next day for same day delivery. Get an email the next day it had been picked up but when speaking to third party courier that it wont be delivered till the next day. Spoke to every person/supervisor and everyone saying they cant expedite it.

On the outbound flight, the aircraft departed with a 30-minute delay. I am writing this review while still on board for the return flight, which is currently delayed by more than one hour, with no clear explanation provided.

Plane late to take off. Lost our suitcase, turns out they didn't even check it in even though we watched the suitcase go through on the belt at Innsbruck Airport. Business class not acceptable. Half of our party were put on Stand by seats which were our children seats. We realised on arrival at Heathrow that we didn't have a ticket label for our suitcase. Spent an hour at lost luggage filling out a missing luggage form after waiting an hour for our other luggage to come onto the belt. The luggage had all our Christmas presents inside. Unlikely to find it. Terrible service.

Overall a very good (but not perfect) experience in BA business. Checkin was quick, friendly, and hassle free. The lounge in Cape Town has been refurbished and is a nice space. Food was good. Wines were OK but in line with expectations. Boarding was quick. Seat was was modern and clean. In flight staff were friendly. Evening meal was exceptional - the upgrade to Do & Co food was definitely worth it. IFE worked fine. Headphones worked (they don't always). Good rest. Mostly nice breakfast but the melons were crunchy. Coffee is noticeably "good". Landed 30 minutes early. T5 lounge also refurbished and good. Flight to Manchester good - crew worked really hard to serve us in the 11 minutes available. The flight would be deserving of 10/10 except for the fact that I purchased the CPT > London and London > Manchester flights separately (my plans changed). The first was a points ticket and the second a cash ticket. It turns out BA's IT systems are so antiquated that the tickets could not be merged. This meant my luggage could not be checked through to final destination but collected and rechecked. As the layover was tight at 1h 15m I risked missing the onward flight if I did this, so I had to abandon the idea of a checked bag and that meant not being able to bring Christmas gifts from South Africa as I intended. All very annoying and because BA have not invested enough in their IT and operations to allow you to merge two tickets.

BRU to MAN via LHR and return. The flights were delayed, upon transfer at LHR on BA1374 the 7th December the gate agents were asking people having a carry on bag, that they needed to see one agent through the gate. This lead to a massive queue for customers, regardless if their group was previously called to board. Upon reaching that one agent, we were asked to give it away because the flight was full. Upon boarding, some overhead lockers were empty. I complained about that to the crew, who told me that they have no contact with the gate staff and do not know what they are doing inside the terminal. One of the 2 gate agents came on board to look for a missing passenger and i asked her to look around the lockers, being empty. She snapped back at me saying that it is not them who decide but the crew. The crew had just told me the opposite. Poor legroom on board. At LHR and MAN waiting for someone to arrive and place aircraft stairs, then for a bus to arrive and get us inside the terminal.

Because of something pretty basic like de-icing, the captain informed we lost our slot and flight would be delayed for 1 hr 20mins. What once was an exemplary company is now a shame for the whole country

This recent experience has been the worst customer service I have dealt with. I had to call around eight times over several weeks to get a flight change processed. I was given completely conflicting information each time, offered goodwill gestures that were later denied, and promised multiple call backs that never happened. In the end, I was charged almost 400 euros for a change that should not have cost anything, and even my previously offered seat selection refund was refused. The whole process left me feeling misled, exhausted and genuinely dreading my holiday. I used to trust British Airways, but after this ordeal, I will never book with them again.

Great flight, and what a change from the American Airlines outward flight. Here the crew were friendly, cheerful, engaged, and really doing their best. Welcomed on board, and throughout the flight the crew were present, upbeat, and enjoying what they did. Served welcome glass of prosecco before takeoff. Very generous with their drinks - I ordered a Gin and Tonic and got two bottles of gin, a bottle of wine to go with my meal, and then they served another glass of wine during the meal. The meal was excellent - served on proper china plates with glassware, and was tasty, large and enjoyable. Great selection of IFE. Seat was comfortable and spacious. I felt this was a very good premium economy experience - but most of it all, it was the cheerful staff that made it such a good flight.

I had sworn never again with BA after a flight with chatty cabin crew causing no sleep on the 10+ hour flight to SF from London a couple of years ago - but the number of air miles needed was a lot less than for United, and I convinced myself I'd be sleeping the whole way on a night flight happily tucked into my seat after taking a sleeping pill - debris on the taxiway caused damage to a wheel - the captain updated us frequently (maybe too frequently for people who actually were sleeping, but she said US law mandated updates), but I think the mechanics misled her as well - 45 minutes' delay wound up being 3 1/2 hours - delays for safety reasons are OK of course but then once we were airborne i put down my meal tray since sleep wasn't coming - neither was the meal! over 2 hours after takeoff (it's now 3am pacific time), I gave up and lay down, just as the steward asked if I still wanted my soup! My bags arrived a bit late and then I noticed that instead of the correct Club World label, the counter had put on an economy class label. Never again.

Flying business and not able to check-in online, while BA website clearly says that online check-in is available when routes start in Basel. I raised a complaint, thinking I would get some answers, but I only got a copy/pasted answers most probably generated by AI. I asked for my complaint to be escalated and I have not received any acknowledgement or a response for a week.

Flew to and from St Lucia with BA. On the outbound flight I was scowled at by a female air crew member for asking for another drink for my partner. On the way back, entire rows of people were inadvertently not offered breakfast. The explanation was that we were asleep but we were awake enough to be offered juice or a hot drink. Once again, on enquiring if we might have our breakfasts (and I use the word in its loosest sense) my partner got scowled at and there were raised eyebrows. It's like you should actually as though you're the luckiest person in the world just to be flying BA. Let me tell you, you're not! It's a very budget airline these days and the entire experience is very low cost. A shame.

This was a surprisingly OK experience. The plane was new, seats comfortable but legroom is limited for someone my height (186cm). Food was very good, attendants were very kind and there was a nice atmosphere. We took off on time from LHR and had a delay at MSY waiting for the jetty to be attached. All in all, a nice experience in economy.

We were taking my 90 year old mother to Tenerife for probably her last flight and we had booked a window seat for her so she could see the island when we were in the air. Without notifying us they moved her after she had sat in the seat she was allocated initially and three of the cabin crew stood around her demanding she move in an extremely aggressive manner. If a passenger had behaved in the same way they would have been removed from the flight, but despite my complaint to BA it appears bullying is ok if you are wearing a BA uniform! Appalling behaviour and complaints process almost useless as they are offering my 90 year old mother a voucher to fly somewhere else! No apology no customer service BA are a disgrace

Delayed departure but arrival almost on time. The crew were terribly disorganised and inattentive. Drinks not offered for lunch. The food was okay though. Rather lot of turbulence which meant the seat belt sign was on but nobody really cared which felt dangerous.

First flight diverted - Oct 25 BA524 not BAs fault necessarily. And at least our gate was the B44 so a jetway was provided. Second flight good except bus gate arrival on my return from Rome and this was my umpteenth bus arrival of 2025. Do better. If I knew BA was going to be cheap, especially at its main hub, I would have flown with Vueling who almost always uses jetways at its Gatwick base

Two hours of hell seated at the very back of the aircraft with no windows. To make matters worse a family of 6 with three of the worst behaved children I have ever witnessed on a flight. Non stop screaming the entire flight. On child even got out of her Seat as the plane hit the tarmac and the flight attendants said nothing to the parents. This is not ok. I was shaken after that experience. Highlife cafe orders also cancelled.

My overall experience was good. The table was large enough for me to use my laptop comfortably. The food quality was average but acceptable. The only frustrating point was that the power socket was quite loose for my US adapter. It kept slipping out frequently so I was not able to use it to charge my phone. I believe a UK adapter would fit much better.

Unable to check in and book seats due to BA website crashing, When finally got in to check in only seat 30F was left. This seat is unsuitable for use with restricted head, shoulder and leg room. On boarding despite only having one small backpack (laptop sized) between two of us we were told rudely that it nay have to go under my seat if other passengers needed to put their bags in the locker. I was told that it would go under the seat in front despite the fact that there was barely space to get my legs under the seat in front. This is the most uncomfortable seat I have ever sat in . On the return journey, was charged three times for the same item due to cabin crew being unable to operate a card machine competently. Now going from pillar to post trying to get a refund as noone in BA seems to have any interest in taking responsibility to sort a problem out and would rather just get it off their desk. Poor comfort, rude staff, inconsistent application of luggage policies and a complete lack of customer service

Was scheduled to fly to Ghana on the 31st July 2025 from Gatwick Airport on a flight. BA 2067. After checking in and boarding the plane, we were kept waiting on the plane for more than 4 hours. We were told that a couple were sick and could not fly, so their luggage was being taken off the aeroplane. Then we were told they were trying to find a pilot, and then informed that the plane could not go that night as the Ghana airport closes at 11 pm. So we were told that the flight has been delayed due to the difficulties highlighted above and that we had to disembark and asked to collect all our luggage and then to re check the luggage the following morning for an alternate flight the following morning. None of the passengers were offered any drinks or refreshments whilst waiting on the plane. This experience has diminished any confidence in flying BA in future. This is a poor service and unacceptable as BA is the only direct flight to Ghana, often delays and can cancel flights, and refuses to pay any compensation due to their poor service. I have decided not to fly BA in future.

British Airways economy cabin A320 is some kind of joke. I couldn't fit in the seat. If it wasn't for a fact that tje middle sit was empty, I don't know how I would get to Warsaw on the flight. I complain about our domestic airlines, Air Canada in particular, but AC is like 5star in comparison to British Airways A320. After this experience I will never book British Airways for european flights. I would give zero, if not for the crew that was very friendly, what a shame that they give them that kind of plane to work with.

A 45 minute queue to enter the lounge (needed to do some work, but not possible inside). Lounge on a one in one out policy, dirty inside, poor quality food and for their home hub appalling. Food on board, had short rib pie and mine was truly disgusting. 2 hours after meal service started I moved my tray to another start so I could get out, still there when next meal served. Welcome on board drink and one drink with meal, cabin crew then disappeared for the remainder of the flight. Overall, an airline in decline, unfortunately it is declining from a very low point to start with. Avoid at all costs.

The airline delayed my flight from Dublin causing me to miss my connection. They are refusing to refund my payment for the seat on the basis that I had cancelled the flight. This was not the case because I missed the connection due to their delays. Very poor service. Avoid British Airways.

I booked a flight for my travel on Oct 10, 2025. Went to ba.com and booked a Premium economy seat for $1800. I cannot travel now because of compromised immune system. So, on Sep 6th I went to ba.com and cancelled my ticket and they are going to refund $100.

Flight delayed 1 hr and 8 min. Flight crew friendly enough, however, the fasten seatbelt sign remained on for the entire flight. The issue I have with this is that we were advised by the flight crew that there was turbulence and it was not safe for us to use the toilets. However, it was apparently safe enough for the flight crew to walk around the cabin with food/drink trolleys and serve food (on trays) and drinks (in glasses). There were a number of people in business class at the front of the aircraft who enquired about using the toilets and we were all provided the same explanation. Flight crew were friendly enough, however, the overall experience was uninspiring and we will reassess whether to take this flight again and just drive to/from Heathrow.

My wife and I flew from Vancouver (YVR) to London (LHR) in business class (Club World) on flight BA 0084. Our original seat selection was for nought as they changed the aircraft from a 777-200 to 777-300. Our row 4 seats were moved to row 12. We were not advised of this by BA, I only discovered this when checking our reservation prior to flight. This placed us into a cabin with 11 rows of Club World (there are 76 Club World seats spread over three separate cabins). This large cabin lacks the traditional feel of a business class cabin which in my option, should not be more than 7 rows per section. The main issue with such a large cabin is that personalised service from the flight staff is significantly diminished and this was certainly the case on this flight. Slow to bring out the welcome drinks, towels etc. Their overall demeanour was indifferent and enthusiasm and customer service bordering on indifferent. The male steward I had was not too bad, however, the female stewardess that my wife had was much worse and gave the impression that she would prefer to be anywhere else. Certainly not the standard that I expect as a business class customer. We travel business class often and will seek out other airlines and their business class offerings to compare. We may or may not return to BA.

Excellent flight. Super crew on BA99 on August 30. Food was superb. Plane was clean. Business Class had a solid hard and soft product. Plane left late due to airport issues with a different crippled plane on a taxiway slightly delayed but arrived on time in Toronto. We were a family of 8 and had a great flight. Just wonderful in every aspect.

Flight left and arrived on time. Very good food served in a friendly and efficient way. The crew on board BA347 on the 30th August was the best crew I ever experienced. Flight attendant had noticed that our family of 8 all travelling together are from Canada and his experience had shown that Canadians like Ginger Ale - he therefore had loaded this drink for this flight. What a nice touch.

My friend and I were helped and we would like to say how much of a huge help Dellina was, very friendly and extremely professional showing compassion. We were on standby and worried that we wouldn't be able to get on, this was on the 28th August, we didn't get on the first flight (BA2701- LGW) however one of my friends did but Dellina, had told us of another flight later that day (BA412 - LHR) which we managed to get on, we wouldn't have known about the second flight if it wasn't for Dellina.

As a regular flier in this route my previous experience of food and service has been very mixed with the majority been bad on both counts. However my flight today was on time the crew were very professional and polite and the food was very good why can't it be like this all the time. However the seats are uncomfortable the wifi is hit and miss and why as a business class passenger are they still charging for seats unless you want to wait till 7 days before flying for seat selection. I choose the route for the flight times and generous luggage allowance but as a regular business class traveller other airlines are streets ahead in their service provision.

We booked four seats to fly to London from Toronto. I can't reclaim the precise details of the booking from BA, but it ran to more than CDN $100 per seat, each way. We had booked specific seats to give our grandson a window seat, and his mother an aisle seat. Come check-in at YYZ, we found our seat choices changed, and we were occupying a row of four seats in the centre of the aircraft, clearly not what we had paid for. I understand that sometimes the airline has to change aircraft, and that was obviously the case here, but I decided that as BA hadn't honoured my paid seat selection that they should give me my seat reservation money back. I made a claim with BA using their online claims process, but my claim was denied, on the grounds that we had taken the flight, albeit not in the seats we'd paid for. I didn't think they'd read the claim because I wasn't claiming that I couldn't fly, just that they'd taken money for specific seats that they now couldn't supply. BA has subsequently ignored my arguments and doesn't reply to my messages. So, if you're booking with BA, be aware that they can and will fail to honour any choices you make, and pay for. I feel as if I've been ripped off; why would I pay for specific seats if the airline have no intention of supplying said seats? Maybe this is why BA can advertise "lower fares" than their competitors.

BA 823 on 9th August 2025 from Dublin to London Heathrow Airport was an absolute pleasure! The check-in staff were not just efficient but also friendly. Boarding was well managed and the flight took off a little earlier than anticipated due to efficient boarding. Although a short flight, the crew worked incredibly hard and the captain was a good natured and clearly humorous. His announcements were friendly, light hearted and informative. He was very professional and greeted passengers as we disembarked and is a credit to British Airways. The flight actually arrived 25 minutes ahead of schedule! I am glad I tried BA again after a pause and based on this experience I have had my faith in BA restored!

Spent 1.5 hours in the check-in queue. The queue went outside the terminal area. There were plenty of Gatwick Airport personnel monitoring the situation as it would reflect badly on them. No BA staff available. Mediocre flight and cabin staff but at least the flight was on time. Only a packet of biscuits were offered for refreshments on a 4.25 hours flight. BA used to offer a small bottle of water as well which now seems to have been withdrawn. Will be choosing another airline in future even if a stop is involved. Very disappointing BA.

Flight was one hour late, meaning public transport options upon arrival in London were severely limited and expensive. The whole reason I had selected to fly this route rather was to avoid a difficult journey into central London but th delay removed the advantage of picking British Airways. USB plugs at my seat did not work inflight.

I have been calling them multiple times 4 days passed since my journey ended but I still don't have my check-in bags with me. 1st day of calling- they asked me to wait for 24-48 hours. 2nd day of calling they said my luggage report was not registered yet (I did it with the airport staff of BA: why it didn't work? 3rd day they said we have escalated your case and the bags seem to be still in London where my luggage was deboarded from the flight. 4th call- Ma'am, we have escalated the case to the Dublin airport and london airport you will surely get an update by EOD And I am .

Cabin crew not help us when we asked why our paid seats had been changed by British Airways and requested to be accommodated in the type of seats we had paid for. We had paid for an aisle and window seat upfront but they changed these to rear window and middle seats. Our request was very polite. Asked the airline for a refund for the amount paid for the seats but not entertained.

Our BA Airbus 380 premium economy section had outdated-looking personal videos. And unfortunately, halfway through a 10-hour flight, the video systems for all of the center seats of the premium economy section stopped working. Staff couldn't resolve the issue, got everyone's names and said there would be something sent to make up for the loss. We ended up getting 20 pounds per person! Given the amount one pays for premium economy, and that the personal entertainment system is a material part of the experience, and given the length of the flight and associated outage, the compensation was token. I would beware folks particularly for BA A380 flights - its pretty old gear and little sense of value for passengers' loss of services. (My 777 plane on the roundtrip was far better.) Staff were competent though not warm. Flight was on time. Food was passable. Leg space is the main value (and that presumably they cannot botch midflight!). I will say I recommend BA, but based on the entire roundtrip, not just this flight, and with the caveat that one could find better, and unfortunately worse.

They lost my bag and took 20 days to find it. The entire time their customer service was incompetent giving me consistently incorrect information which would change with every call. Customer service representatives were rude and not helpful to me. Flight was below average, my food was not good and seats were tight.

Decided to use point to upgrade to business after visiting family in the UK. I have to say British Airways Business Class was up there with the best of them. Comfortable seating, great service from the crew and with a smile, and great food. On the whole I found the experience comfortable and worth the points upgrade and will consider flying them again.
Mumbai check in is not so helpful. I asked to put my Alaska frequent flyer and he only put the first leg. I was not able to get an aisle seat . Boarding in Mumbai was chaotic.
BA First lounge at T5 very busy as usual. Flight departed early and arrived 20 min ahead of schedule. Flight uneventful; good catering for this 45 min flight; recommended
Terrible experience. No respect to priority boarding, crowded buses to take us to plane, without to mention the waiting time we had to wait inside the switched off bus with NO air conditioning.

Check-in was slow with only one staff member checking in economy class in the initial period. After passport control, in the security check area, the flight was shown as cancelled. Back we, and others, went to the check-in counter where the staff seemed uninterested in the confusion caused. "It's not cancelled," they said, "Go back to security" where the flight was still shown as cancelled. Once aboard the cancelled but not cancelled flight the seats were wide enough but legroom was limited. Water and an oat bar were served. The flight arrived on time and baggage appeared promptly.

Check in was smooth enough. Boarding was chaotic. We were herded through the gate only to be held for a seemingly never ending period of time outside next to the apron. We are BA silver members and noticed that despite business class being nearly empty we were not offered the chance to move up a class. The seat pocket in front of me full of the previous passenger's rubbish. On arrival at Heathrow, our bags took a long time to reach the belt and plenty arrived before ours even though ours were supposed to be priority.

Although transferring to this flight through Heathrow from Budapest took almost an hour, the flight crew was welcoming and friendly as we boarded at the last minute. I had tried to reserve a vegetarian meal online the day before the flight but couldn't, and asked Sarah, the head flight attendant, if they might be able to provide one. She not only found a delicious meal from Premium, Economy, but was especially caring and helpful throughout the flight. The flight attendants also offered water and juice several times during the flight. I was also impressed with the wide range of entertainment offerings, which included some first-rate films.
We are extremely grateful to the crew of flight BA0058 from Cape Town to Heathrow. They brought us home with such a high level of professionalism, flexibility, and empathy. Thank you so much.

Good points, the cabin crew, they were helpful, professional and mature, Quantity and quality of food, cleanliness of the aircraft which was spotless Picture of a pub in the forward toilet and the flight was on time. BA's T3 lounge is just not anything special, mediocre at best, food options lacking, its Gatwick & T5 lounges are far more superior. On board usual poor seat pitch, the Club Europe product is inconsistent, no hot towels, menu given however food delivered on a trolley in the economy way, all the courses on one tray. No further bar offerings unless one used the call bell. Parked on remote stand at Krakow. On return Krakow - LHR Queued for twenty minutes at the Club Europe check in desk, the non-BA lounge was basic and at the late departure time of the flight, minimal food choices. On boarding Cramped into a bus and walked up on remote stand. No menus or hot towels, however meal orders taken individually and delivered direct from the Galley, seat uncomfortable, no wi-fi. Had to request tea after meal. Again inconsistency in service. The extra cost of Club Europe is hard to justify, there have been improvements in catering, however the product needs to be elevated to justify the cost.

It was a decent flight, reasonable comfortable seat and pilot kept us nicely informed about the flight's progress. BA serve biscuits and a small bottle of water for free. This was ok for me but sandwiches had run out from the in-flight cafe to the disappointment of passengers. Inflight wifi is limited and you have to pay to access music or programmes. BA's offering is well below that of Aegean and this level of service is not suitable for easterly destinations such as Larnaca. So I would certainly fly again with BA to Athens but only in the event Aegean has no seats or the fare is cheaper.

Having had some rough experiences with BA in recent years, I did not look forward to this particular flight. However, it turned out to be a decent trip. The staff were really engaged and seemed to enjoy what they were doing. Food was acceptable, although there has to be other options than pasta or chicken on long-haul flights! Seating was good and the IFE worked well.

This comfortable flight was BA at its best. Excellent start in the Chelsea Lounge with Krug behind the bar. Lounge hosts were welcoming and friendly, food not quite up to par but much better onboard. The First Suite is spacious and comfortable, and the two cabin crew were both experienced, friendly, professional and personable. They sprang to action quickly after takeoff, making beds or serving dinner as required. The menu was excellent with a well cooked beef fillet and delicious salmon starter. The new Nyetimber 1086 is an exceptionally good wine! Overall the service was well relaxed and intuitive. The cabin was comfortably cool and I left the flight feeling refreshed. BA have made some poor choices of late with their loyalty programme, but their staff still shine and they really got it right on this flight.

Punta Cana Terminal B check in was straightforward with separate Club World desks. Agent was polite, issued boarding cards, provided a voucher for the VIP lounge and explained how to find it. No fast track security unless you paid $50 per passenger but that was the airport, not BA. VIP lounge was comfortable but not quiet due to 3 crying babies but that's life! Flight boarding was on time, we were group 2 and it was well managed by gate staff Old style club world seating but the cabin was clean, cabin crew were on hand and offered champagne or orange juice, there was a bottle of water in the drawer with the White Company amenity pack. White Company duvet was clean in a sealed bag. Order for drinks was taken before take off. Drinks were served promptly followed by dinner which we ordered immediately after take off. My starter of cream of leek soup was delicious served with warm bread. I declined the main course as it was late (choice was fillet steak or shrimp linguine). Dessert was chocolate mousse or cheese and biscuits however they found both for me as I didn't have the main. Excellent pinot noir from South Africa, refills were offered. Following dinner I got about 5 hours sleep and found the lay flat bed comfortable but I am pretty small. The duvet and pillow were great. Breakfast was ho hum, no orange juice was offered, bircher muesli was fine, fruit wasn't ripe and was almost inedible. The muffin was very cold and dry, coffee okay. I declined the breakfast baguette. Excellent cabin staff and having read so many negative reviews the experience exceeded my expectations.

I had only 1 bag with me, a carry on trolley. Everyone one in boarding group 3 & 4 were forced to check-in their trolley carry-ons. They asked to take out any laptops, batteries, etc.... The woman at the boarding gate was very rude to me as I was explaining to her that this was my only bag and had nowhere to carry my laptop or other stuff that I need onboard. I tried to explain to her that the bag will not withstand being carried in the hold as it is fragile and showed her a crack from the one time I checked it in before. The bag was visibly small complying with the carry-on bag measurements.

Check in and security at T5 quick. Both Galleries lounges pretty much at capacity, not able to access B gates lounge as short haul, A gates departure Food options reasonable. Bus to aircraft which was quite new. On time departure. Reasonable food and drink options. Pleasant cabin crew. Bags off quickly.

Very good service on this route BA2710 30th March. Cabin crew worked hard, particularly Ivka (?) who was on the go throughout the flight. Everything you would expect of BA (and as it used to be!) Shame the same cannot be said on our recent flight back from Singapore, in Business Class on 11th Feb BA12. Miserable, unhappy and tetchy crew. Too lazy to do anything except sleep! Perhaps BA need to promote some of their short-haul performers, and let the others go.

Flight mainly let down by a disagreeable flight attendant. No queue to check in at Cape Town - good. However checkin agent was unfamiliar with BA size and weight rules for sports bags so had to wait 10 minutes while phone calls were made -- annoying. Lounge was good. Gate service was excellent with organised queues. Seat was good (the new upgraded Club Suite). The zip broke off the amenity kit so it was unusable -- BA cutting corners too much here. Offered a cocktail service which came promptly and the drink was excellent. But no nuts! So I went off to the galley to ask for some nuts or a snack to go with it. I spoke to a male flight attendant who looked at me with utter distaste that I had the temerity to ask for nuts. The he said "where have you come from?". What a bizarre question. I said "seat 8E" to which he responded with a flick of his hand - "go ask her, she's serving you." I was stunned - I have not been treated that way in even the cheapest restaurants, let alone business class on a premium airline. The gentlemen concerned has no place in service or hospitality and should find a different line of work. Anyway, the food was good. The IFE worked fine. WiFi wasn't working. I managed 6.5 hours sleep and we got off the plane promptly despite being at a remote stand, requiring a bus. The luggage took quite a while to arrive. Overall 7/10. Would be 9/10 but for the rude staff member.
Another awful experience by British Airways. This flight was delayed nearly 1 hour. British Airways charges an extortionate amount for their tickets but the service is bad for me.
The service was rude, full of attitude to me, the food is poorly serviced, the cabin during the flight was never cleaned in particularly the toilets.

This flight was a joke. There was four people in business class including myself and my companion. The service was outrageous. The crew was too busy flirting with the captain and where she was going for the day off, instead of paying attention in the cabin.

The seats were excellent, with a feel of much more room than the official seat pitch (I am 6ft 1in). We could sleep for a couple of hours (daytime flight), with the blinds down as they should be (no point booking a window seat in my view). I focus on seat quality much more than smiley faces and food (the food was middling, and the second meal, before landing, was distinctly sub-par).

I flew from Amsterdam to Las Vegas with a layover in Heathrow in November 2024. The day we were flying the weather wasn't great. Since I was on business I really needed to get to Las Vegas, we anticipated on it and checked early if our flight was still leaving. We would have had ample time to catch an earlier flight to Heathrow or even take the train when we checked. According to google our flight was delayed and we would miss our connection. According to the staff of British airways the flight was not delayed and there was no reason for panic. When we got to the airport there was still nothing wrong with our connection. An hour before we were supposed to leave it was announced that the plane wasn't there yet and we would have a major delay. We called customer service and they told us to just go to London and see from there. We wanted some kind of assurance that we could be placed in a hotel since we would not be making our connecting flight and they refused to give those. In the end we found a direct flight the next day and convinced British airways to book that for us. Even though they wanted to connect us through 3 additional layovers.. This resulted in approximately a 24 hour delay in our trip. On our way back home they lost our luggage at the gate and took approximately 2 hours to find it at a wrong gate. On the way back we tried to check in through the online portal. My colleague was able to check in just fine but I couldn't. I was afraid I was overbooked and contacted customer service 3 times. When I got to the airport I was overbooked and the ground staff had the nerve to tell me it was my fault for not checking in online. Since we were seated in premium economy I could be moved to regular economy but that does mean someone in economy was bumped off the plane. When we got to London our flight back to Amsterdam was delayed. This was because there were disabled people on board of the plane still and there were not enough wheelchairs to get them off. It took approximately 2 hours before boarding could begin. When we finally boarded we were told we needed a new pilot because the old pilot had now made too many hours waiting around to still fly us to Amsterdam. Arriving in Amsterdam they had left my luggage in Las Vegas so I needed to wait for another week before that was given back to me. Afterwards I have made a claim as soon as possible for my delays and hotel costs, it's been almost 3 months and they still haven't replied. Every time I contact them they claim they have such a huge backlog that it takes long to process them.

I have never travelled with British airways before and this is the first time I chose to travel with BA due to the cheapest fare available during this time but I was bit unsure if I can enjoy my travel journey due to mixed reviews. I would like to express my extreme joy and satisfaction travelling with this amazing airline. I haven't seen such a great, efficient and friendly service by the cabin crew. I would like to personally thanks Ellie and Adam who were not only very professional but very kind too. Food served was delicious and the drinks were good too. I can say that I thoroughly enjoyed this flight and do not hesitate to recommend to anyone to try it

Terrible overall, medium service and the flight was delayed. There was no help at all to reschedule a connecting flight. The customer support was terrible and the request for compensation is still pending after one year.

London Heathrow to Male In new business class. BA continues to get its mojo back starting with a classy lounge serving innovative, and interesting, quality pre-flight food (beetroot scotch eggs?). Excellent wine (Whispering Angel). Presentation of on-board food has always been a bit hit and miss with BA, but on this occasion it was tasty and OK. Friendly and efficient on board crew. Smile, treat them respectfully, and as equals. On time flight and early arrival. Only awarding a 9 because we were bussed from A-C gates, otherwise a really enjoyable experience.
Very good flight following an equally good flight to Rome. Good food (especially on an evening flight) and aircraft early both ways. Just what short haul should be.

An hour's delay due to late arrival of the incoming aircraft. The captain was a particularly able communicator who kept us in touch with the situation. We got freebie upgrades to emergency exit seats from a friendly member of the crew. In the end we were only 30 minutes behind schedule in a relatively comfortable elderly plane. Pretty stress free.

British airways lost bags in LHR then found them. Sent to Cologne where it sat for two days before they told me, but no one was there to give it to me. I spent 10 days in Europe without a bag, bought clothes. BA refused to reimburse me. They closed the case 10 days after i returned to the states when my bag showed up at my front door. They wont let you talk to management, they say they email mail you but they don't then you call customer service. they say they will escalate it but you will never know. they don't update the claims or the forms.

The check in process and reward/loyalty program is a mess. I am never able to get points, even when trying it through a partner airline. Unfortunately for work I have to travel with them sometimes. This time, the flight was delayed.

We flew in November 2023, but it took this long to seek a satisfactory response from BA, which we ultimately never received. BA refused to re-book my son and me at no cost that day due to lack of Underground service / alternate service. BA forced us to buy new tickets and never admitted that they subjected us to disparate treatment. I will not be flying or recommending BA again.

After an excellent flight on a 777 CPT to LHR the return was not as good. BA have moved the Business Class checkin from one end of the hall to the other at T5 for no apparent reason so a nice long walk to check in. Fast Track security was very slow (15 minutes). The indicator board suggested the South Lounge was "half full" but when I went it was uncomfortably full and it is still tatty as not refurbished, so I went to the B Pier lounge instead. Much better except as usual the staff are sort of trying to pack up early and have a bizarre way of refilling the food containers which involves actually removing them to the kitchen (which means they are gone a lot of the time) rather than replenishing them customer side. Very employee-centric behaviour. Time for the flight so down to the transit to take us to the C Gates. Except the transit had decided not to stop any more at the B Gates so we watched five maybe seven transits pass through without stopping. Eventually me and a group of maybe 15 other passengers of mixed ages decided to descend to the walkway and run all the way to the C Gates. We all arrived soaked in sweat - not a nice start to a long business class flight. The A380 is spacious but the seat is outdated now and in urgent need of replacement. IFE was not working and had to be rebooted. The headphone prong was bent so headphones not working. The USB port was not working. Drinks were brought out promptly. Starter (salmon) was delicious - truly excellent. Beef was tough ... I think a bad piece of meat rather than badly cooked. Wines were good. Cheese was average to good. Staff were friendly. Good night's sleep. Breakfast good. The recheck experience at JNB is a huge hassle - there is a giant screen saying "Domestic recheck" and a queue but when you get to the front of the queue you are told it is SAFAIR only and not for SAA, BA's local partner. What a hassle. Why aren't we warned or told this ... loads of BA passengers making the same mistake. Overall 5/10. It's the little things that would make this better: fast track actually fast track. Refurbish the South Lounge. Have food replenishment in the passenger area, not the kitchen; make sure the transits stop, even late in the evening; refurbish the A380s; ask Do & Co (who are generally excellent by the way) to monitor meat quality rigorously.

Pretty good flight but still some small things that can be improved. Check in was quick. Lounge was good - tasty food and well chosen wines. Disappointingly they had not secured a gate so we had to bus to the aircraft and it was all a hot scrum. I got the last bus to avoid the crush. Emirates, Turkish, Lufthansa, Qatar all had planes on gates ... why not BA? Penny-pinching? Then it turned out the cabin crew forgot about those on the last bus so I had to ask for a welcome drink. It came and the champagne was actually cold. Well done BA ... first time they managed to serve champagne cold in my 10 years of flying with them. Big improvement. Cabin and seat were lovely as always (I greatly prefer to the Emirates white/gold bling). Drinks service was prompt. IFE was good. Starter (trout) was OK. Main (chicken) was excellent. Cheese was sold not cold (as it should be). Wines were excellent. We were not disturbed through the night so got a good sleep on a comfy bed. Cabin was a bit too warm though for my personal preference. Was woken up (as asked) and served a tasty breakfast. Small detail - as it is impossible to get water to 100C at altitude maybe BA could warm the ceramic coffee cups so coffee retains its heat a bit longer? Pouring not quite hot coffee into a nice (but cold) china mug means it is lukewarm instantly. Off the plane in record time (2 minutes) after parking. Bags were waiting for us on the belt. Excellent work by the ground staff. Overall 8/10. Improvement points: gate not bus to the plane; don't forget passengers on the last bus or who board late (but well before pushback). Standout cabin crew member was "Miguel" - what a star.

British Airways is absolute rubbish. I had to fly to Amsterdam for an urgent appointment. The flight was cancelled last minute presumably due to bad weather. They've kept us at the gate saying the plane couldn't land while literally every plane from that airport was taking off and landing with zero issues. There was another KLM flight to Amsterdam scheduled to depart at the same time. It took off on time and another KLM flight to Amsterdam later the evening also took off without any problems. It's just the one operated by British Airways was cancelled because of 'the bad weather'. Apparently, the weather was so bad that every plane could land and take off successfully apart from theirs. I had to rebook myself on the Eurostar the next day and would still miss the important appointment that I intended to go to Amsterdam for. All thanks to British Airways.

The flight time was changed at the last minute without warning and no assistance was provided by the ground staff (3rd party agents) regarding the impact for the delay, nor was any help forthcoming from the phoneline. Nobody in the airline wants to take responsibility for anything. This is fundamentally an unreliable airline. Onboard service was poor and not even as good as some low cost airlines.

I'm so fraustrated. My flight was cancelled last minute, which wasn't the end of the world, even though the earliest I could get re-booked was three days later. It's the insane saga of events that proceeded to claim the compensation that I'm legally entitled to according to EU rules. Used their claims page and all was OK. It was from there that it became incomprehensibly frustrating. My case was closed but no confirmation of what the conclusion was or any money. I tried calling but kept being lead in circles; customer services can't speak to the claims team, the claims team can't be spoken to directly, customer service don't have access to the claims team's system and so on. 4 calls later and 'nothing could be done'. I had to throw my toys out of the pram on the last call and someone finally updated me. I thought that was the end; they had confirmed the claim and that I would be transferred what I was due. And then, they got the amount wrong. I wrote to they to highlight this and they said that they would rectify it. Almost 1 month since the original flight was cancelled and still haven't received what is owed to me as compensation for my wife and son. I have sent two more emails in the last two days and I've yet to get a response. It is criminal that they are not adhering to the aviation rules that dictate compensation for cancelled flights. Terrible customer service and honestly can't belive that BA are capable of such awful service.

British Airways stranding my wife and I at Heathrow Airport for 2.5 days, with no access to our baggage. We we told by airline employees to purchase any necessities (toiletries, refreshments, etc.) and we'd be reimbursed. That claim was denied, with BA claiming that weather was the reason for the delay (an outright lie since every other airline in London was flying on-time). We were unable to to anything besides stand in lines for vouchers, stand in lines for shuttles, stand in line for reservations, etc. for 48+ hours. It was an absolute nightmare and I will never fly BA again.

This flight was British Airways at its very best. The flight attendants were outstanding - processional, attentive and helpful. The food was very good and the seat/lie flat bed was very comfortable. I love to smart design of the A350 Club World cabin. Wonderful flight home!

Disappointing service, plane interior and terribly incompetent customer service I booked my flight directly through BA's website. Soon after I started to get emails saying my selected seats (I paid extra for the selection) had been changed by BA without any reason given and I was directed to the website. There I found no information on the said seat change. This happened several times (I had 4 flights altogether). The website seems to be a digital dinosaur. The first leg of my flight was fine, until I discovered in the transfer area at Heathrow that I forgot my new laptop onboard. Immediately I contacted BA's so called Customer Service (what an oxymoron), which basically said they can not do anything, I would have to wait until the cleaners (working for a contractor) would have finished their job and hope they would discover the laptop and return it to so called Lost & Found at the airport. BA's customer service said they couldn't contact their colleagues in the terminal/gate were the plane was still and let them know there was a lost laptop by seat no 27A of the plane (yes I told them exactly were the laptop was). They wouldn't take any contact details either to notify me if and when the laptop would be returned and they refused to register the incident. They simply had no interest in assisting me and didn't even make an attempt to pretend they did. Communication via their online customer service was poor, and they didn't even respond to my messages. In the end I emailed the representative at Heathrow and he replied with a message form his supervisor (which did not reveal his name): "It is not the duty of British Airways to find lost property on behalf of our passengers, however if you would like to dispute this you can contact customer relations online with further feedback." They took no responsibility and referred me to Smartecarte, which is the contractor cleaning their planes and apparently collecting lost items at Heathrow. I have not received the laptop, worth 2 thousand GBP, back now 3 weeks later. The flights between London and Cape Town (~12 hours), were unpleasant. The flight attendants were seemingly unenthusiastic about their job, it took up to an hour to collect the trash after the meal, which also was distributed extremely slowly. Food was not good. Boarding was slow and inefficient. Drinks were only offered twice (otherwise you'd have to ask for it especially) on this long flights. The seats were of fabric, uncomfortable and room too scarce to relax and sleep. All in all flying with British Airways was disappointing and I will not be keen on flying with them again.

A transit visa is required for my partner to transit via London to Iceland. So I had to buy a separate ticket for her via another airline. When we reach Iceland I emailed British Airways telling then she won't be using her return ticket and requested for a partial refund. 2 days later. I received an email from customer service that I need to contact one of their service centres via the provided link. I replied to say the link only goes to a page with various British landline phone numbers to call and explained that I am overseas then and it will not be practical to do this via international calls. They replied to say I can only do this by contacting the service centres. So the airline end up taking my money regardless.

Flight cancelled, not refunding our money saying we took the flight that never happened. Not refunding the new flights we booked, hotels, food while we were stranded. Did not provide food or water while waiting for hours on tarmac. Will not provide information as to why they aren't refunding the flight that never happened. Saying there is no more information.

I had visa issues, and hence, was debarred from flying. The ground staff at Mumbai was excellent (a woman named Brinelle) was very helpful and understanding. I had to rebook my tickets, and while the original journey was consisting of 3 legs, BA forced me to rebook the entire ticket, because their system did not allow them to rebook just that one leg (even though there was a gap of 13 days between the two legs, not like they were connecting flights). The telephone operator was rude, took 45 minutes and kept saying she needed 3-4 more minutes to give me clarity. It was horrendous. The final price they offered me for rebooking 2 of the 3 legs was much more than the original fare for all 3 legs. She was torturous, BA was horrendous because the website does not allow you to do all this. A very poor experience, in all.

I paid for seats 80 A and B on my flight from Heathrow to Boston on the A380, paying for premium economy seats. Upon arrival at the airport the ticket agent said I was not healthy enough to sit in the purchased seats due to being too old I presume (65) since there is no other reason I can find I could not sit in the exit seating. I am healthy enough to walk 10-12 miles a day and have adequate upper body strength. Attempting to convince her just got us stuck in a cattle call seat, at the rear of the aircraft, second floor and in the middle two seats of the row. We were told our money would be refunded immediately for the "inconvenience". After several weeks I recontacted BA and they said the complaint went to the wrong section and they were forwarding it to the next section. 6 weeks later and we still have not heard any updates except for a computer response stating most refunds were returned in 3 weeks, keep waiting. The plane then had ground difficulties and needed a quick repair. They completed that 30 minutes later and boarded the flight. The captain then came on and said it looks like they forgot to order the ground crew to back us out of the terminal and we needed to wait another 30 minutes. We were not able to make up for the lost time in the air. We landed 1.5 hours later than scheduled, wreaking havoc with our next flight.

I was very impressed with their efficient boarding, the relatively (compared to Air Canada) comfortable seats and the quality of the food. Drinks and snacks frequently offered. Overall a no fuss, no bother experience.

I have been flying BA for over 15 years. I was an American Airlines FF and gave it up for BA. I am a Gold member on BA and have been for over 10 years. Here are the things I have noticed over the last 5 years on BA. the Flight attendants are getting lazier and complacent, from cleaning bathrooms to serving meals. The food on BA has deteriorated to the point of not being able to eat the garbage they give you and having gold status is almost meaningless in the big scheme of things. I have NEVER been able to upgrade to business or first using the AVIOS points I have accumulated on a transcon flight.
